fragments.text: Target edition: 17 October 2026. Gauge is a US agency professional services automation product for the owner or operations lead of a 5–40 person design, marketing, software agency or consultancy. It connects estimates and retainers, staffing, time and expenses, delivery evidence and invoicing to a live margin, utilization and cash forecast. A buyer can replace Kantata, Harvest + Forecast, Scoro or Teamwork.com, or choose Gauge over Productive, Rocketlane or Float, without maintaining a separate spreadsheet for the core agency job.

This is the destination product, not a description limited to today's release. Missing implementation is work to build, not a reduction in scope. Every clause gives the buyer behavior and an acceptance journey through a public screen, API, command, download or provider callback. Network/provider sandboxes may substitute at the paid/network edge in tests; no application mock or fabricated completion satisfies a clause. [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) repeats every journey and its current status. The final Status table cites implementation and tests, not a claim of live agency, provider or hosted proof.
| Category | Professional services automation (PSA) / agency management software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Kantata, Harvest + Forecast, Scoro, Teamwork.com, Productive, Rocketlane, Float |
| First buyer | Owner or operations lead of a 5–40 person US agency or consultancy, working in USD with W-2 employees, 1099 contractors, project leads, finance and an outside accountant |

The complete job runs from pipeline and accepted scope through retainers, phase budgets, resource requests, calendars and delivery, to approved actuals, issued invoices, collection and an explained portfolio forecast. Client collaboration, mobile/desktop time, follow-up, migration and accounting reconciliation belong to that job. PSA-specific estimates and project work remain in Gauge; neighboring products remain separate as BOUNDARY-003 specifies.
New installations start empty. The owner enters real records or imports authorized source data. Existing demo/test fixtures are never a substitute for agency migration or live-provider evidence.

US-first means USD new-business defaults, US billing addresses and payment terms, sales-tax provider handoff, card/ACH through the agency merchant account and IANA timezones with daylight-saving handling. Exact money carries currency; durations remain whole seconds, separate from billing increments. Clients and engagements may bill in another ISO currency under SETUP-005. No implicit FX: conversion uses only SETUP-003's owner-approved, effective-dated rates, and historical AUD records never silently convert.

Every page, read, write, API, download and callback checks current native or scoped integration authority at the handler; writes recheck grants in the committing transaction. Revocation takes effect at the next request. Browser writes check origin, credentials stay private, and restored data never imports authority.

Every write uses a request key. Same key and content yields the original outcome; different content is refused. External commands also carry stable source/action identity and reconcile uncertain results before another attempt.

Approval binds exact record revisions, terms, recipients and computed effects. Changed inputs require renewed approval. Approved commercial versions, frozen rates and issued artifacts keep their history; corrections append linked records with actor and reason.

Owner holds finance authority and alone manages grants. Finance sees private rates/costs and authorizes money; leads control assigned delivery and staffing; staff confirm their own work. Detailed target roles and delegation are GOVERN-001 through GOVERN-004.

Agents prepare; the appropriate person decides. Agent grants cannot self-approve, commit staffing, promise client changes or bill. A bounded policy can authorize only its stated follow-up action after the required human decisions. Sources and imported notes are inert data, never instructions or authority. Existing agents receive no private amounts; future least-privilege financial analysis requires a separately authorized finance scope.
Unknown capacity, missing costs, stale connectors, pending ACH and unconfirmed evidence remain explicit. Successful submission or job invocation never proves delivery, payment or forecast recovery.

The seventeen released clause IDs remain intact. The original AUD pilot (historical baseline: 17 October 2026) now supports a saved agency currency and timezone, with USD and America/Los_Angeles defaults for new installations. Setup offers USD, AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP, NZD, CHF and SGD, all with two decimal minor units. The forward migration infers the agency currency from existing stored money without rewriting amounts, revisions or approved artifacts. Native billing remains CSV billing-packet preparation, with currency mismatches refused and no FX conversion. `done` for the published core does not mean the full SETUP-001, invoice/accounting, retainer, integration or forecasting targets are complete.

**ENGAGEMENT-001 — Set up agreed work.** Finance creates clients and people (with work timezone and contractor flag), an engagement with its responsible lead, assigned members, agreed scope and work timezone, and its tasks and milestones.
**Acceptance evidence:** `ENGAGEMENT-001 real empty account to scoped engagement`.

**BUDGET-001 — Agree terms and change orders.** A lead or finance drafts hourly or fixed-fee terms (budget, effort, billing rounding, reason) and approves the exact version; an approved version cannot change, and a change order is a new version beside it.
**Acceptance evidence:** `BUDGET-001 immutable approved terms and additive change orders`.

**RATE-001 — Keep rates by effective date.** Finance adds person/service cost and bill rates as effective-dated, immutable versions; approving time freezes the rate that applied, so adding today's rate never rewrites past work.
Rates stay private to finance.
**Acceptance evidence:** `RATE-001 effective-dated private rates`; `TIME-002 return, correction and approval of exact revisions` (later rate leaves approved economics unchanged).
**CAPACITY-001 — See next month's capacity.** People maintain dated working calendars (including contractor availability) and leave; leads allocate staff as tentative or committed.
Gauge shows daily available, committed, tentative and remaining time, flags conflicts on committed work and treats a missing calendar as unknown, not zero.
**Acceptance evidence:** `CAPACITY-001 working calendar, leave and separate tentative staffing`; Forecast import `tests/gauge-forecast.mjs`.
**TIME-001 — Record time.** Staff record manual intervals or run a persistent timer, with engagement, task, service, notes, billable flag and explicit IANA timezone.
Overlapping intervals and a second running timer are refused.
**Acceptance evidence:** `TIME-001 persistent timer, exact manual duration, parallel exclusion and idempotence`.
**TIME-002 — Approve and correct time.** Staff submit; the lead returns with a reason or approves the exact revision; approved time is reopened only through an audited correction and approved again.
**Acceptance evidence:** `TIME-002 return, correction and approval of exact revisions`.

**COST-001 — Record expenses with receipts.** Staff add project expenses with receipt files and a reimbursable flag; the lead returns or approves; receipts are fixed at submission and only their owner or finance can download them.
**Acceptance evidence:** `COST-001 expense receipt custody, exact approval and attachment privacy`.

**ECONOMICS-001 — Reconcile the engagement.** Finance sees the latest approved budget against approved actual time and cost, billable value and remaining effort, with the source IDs of entries missing a cost or bill rate.
Others see hours without private costs.
**Acceptance evidence:** `ECONOMICS-001 approved actual cost and remaining effort`.

**BILLING-001 — Draft a billing packet.** Finance selects approved, unbilled hourly work, approved reimbursable expenses or an approved fixed-fee milestone; the draft reserves those exact source revisions, and a concurrent second reservation of the same source fails.
**Acceptance evidence:** `BILLING-001 concurrent source reservations and fixed-fee eligibility`.

**BILLING-002 — Approve and export once.** Finance approves the exact draft, which fixes its lines and CSV artifact with source IDs, revisions, durations, rates and rounding; formula-like text is escaped; repeated downloads return the same bytes; a correction is a linked adjustment packet, never an overwrite.
**Acceptance evidence:** `BILLING-002 exact approval, formula-safe repeated exports and linked correction`.

**REVIEW-001 — Review the week's exceptions.** The Review page lists missing time against calendars, overspend, capacity conflicts, approved unbilled work, missing bill rates and decisions due (including agent proposals awaiting this person), each linked to its source record.
**Acceptance evidence:** `REVIEW-001 grounded decisions, missing time and capacity exceptions`.

**ACCESS-001 — See only permitted work.** Staff see their own work on assigned engagements, leads approve only engagements they lead, private costs and rates stay with finance, and only the owner grants or revokes access;
revocation takes effect on the next request, and unauthenticated or unauthorized direct transport calls are refused.
**Acceptance evidence:** `ACCESS-001 native personas, scoped data and direct transport denials`; `ACCESS-001 revocation and minimal replay acknowledgements`.

**MOVE-001 — Process supplied Harvest exports and leave whole.** Finance previews a Harvest export package (dry run, no writes), reconciles independent client and month totals, applies it in bounded journaled batches, rolls back a partial import, re-imports without duplicates and undoes untouched imported records; edited records refuse undo.
`rer export` and `rer import` restore the complete dataset into an empty install and refuse corrupt archives or occupied destinations.
See [MOVE-IN.md](MOVE-IN.md).

**Acceptance evidence:** `MOVE-001 Harvest preview, partial rollback, native reconciliation, idempotence and untouched undo`; `MOVE-001 complete D1 archive restore, corruption and occupied refusal`; browser journey export → fresh clone → import.

**AGENT-001 — Time reconstruction.** An agent drafts a time entry for a person from cited, consented evidence (for example a calendar entry), noting any ambiguous client match; only that person confirms the actual interval and billability, which creates their own draft to submit.
**Acceptance evidence:** `AGENT-001 time reconstruction: the agent drafts, only the person confirms actual time`.

**AGENT-002 — Resourcing.** An agent offers up to five tentative staffing alternatives with rationale; the page shows each alternative's effect on the person's remaining capacity and conflicts (and, for finance, estimated cost and billable value); the lead approves one, which becomes a tentative allocation.
Agents cannot propose committed staffing.

Exact semantics (21 October 2026): an alternative is one person over an inclusive date window; the page shows the person's open hours and conflict dates before and after, as if the alternative were committed.

Finance alone also sees the estimated cost and *billable value*: every day of the window priced like a FINANCE-006 allocation day (the bill rate effective that day under RATE-002 precedence with withdrawn cards excluded, overtime premium then write-down after the person's other bookings, rounded half up per day, in the engagement currency); internal work reads "Not billable: internal work", and a day with no bill rate or a bill rate in another currency makes the figure "Unknown" with its reason, never zero.
Leads and agents see no cost or billable value.
**Acceptance evidence:** `AGENT-002 resourcing: tentative alternatives only, the lead approves one`.

**AGENT-003 — Billing preparation.** An agent proposes the source lines for a packet; Gauge refuses unapproved, already allocated, duplicated or rate-less sources at preparation; finance approves, which drafts the exact packet, then approves the packet as in BILLING-002.
The agent never sees amounts.
**Acceptance evidence:** `AGENT-003 billing preparation: eligibility checked, finance approves the exact packet`.

**AGENT-004 — Delivery exceptions.** An agent drafts a change-order brief grounded in exceptions; the lead declines it with a reason or approves it, which drafts a change-order version whose terms the lead then approves (BUDGET-001).
An agent can withdraw its own open proposal.
**Acceptance evidence:** `AGENT-004 delivery exceptions: change-order briefs are declined or approved by the lead`.
**SETUP-001 — US agency setup.** The owner sets the legal business, US billing address, USD base (reporting) currency, EIN reference, fiscal year, workweek and IANA timezones.
Money uses explicit ISO currency and exact minor units; old AUD records keep their currency and never silently convert.
USD is the new-install default; client and engagement billing in other currencies follows SETUP-005.

Current semantics (23 October 2026, conservative default pending ct): the owner alone saves the profile (first-run form or Access), each change keeping its reason and revision history; the legal business and US address are visible to the owner and finance, the EIN to the owner only and never on a document, export or audit view for anyone else; the fiscal year is a start month; an import in another currency declares `currencyPolicy: keep-source-currency` (conversion is never an import option); the owner approves forward-only, effective-dated rates (rate, source, reason, approver) and the consolidation read converts each approved time or expense amount at the rate effective on its date, naming rate and date beside every total, leaving an amount with no approved rate unconverted and the total withheld, never zero.

**Acceptance evidence:** Start empty, configure a New York agency, quote and invoice USD work across a daylight-saving change; import an old AUD record and require an explicit conversion policy before consolidation.

**SETUP-002 — Client and contact workspace.** Finance keeps legal clients, billing and project contacts, addresses, tax and exemption references, payment terms, PO requirements, tags and client custom fields (SETUP-004); search and merge preserve linked engagements and external identities.

Finance-set Net N payment terms (0–365 days on the client record, used by the FINANCE-002 cash forecast) are shipped and stay: the client's Net N is used when set, and "Net 30 assumed" appears only while it is unset.
A merge keeps the surviving client's payment terms, and a conflict between the two clients' terms is an explicit finance choice at merge, never silent (ct, 20 October 23:45Z).

The exact rules (21 October 2026): finance or the owner saves on the client record a legal name; billing and project contacts (name, optional email and phone); billing, legal and project addresses (line 1, optional line 2, city, optional state and postal code, and a two-letter ISO country, US when left blank); a tax ID reference and exemption-certificate references (references only: taxability, provider calculation and the exemption workflow are INVOICE-005's); whether invoices need a PO and the client's PO numbers; tags; and external IDs written `system:id`.
A field left out of a save keeps its saved value; every change is a new revision with history and a GOVERN-005 audit entry.
An external identity (a recorded `system:id`, or an import's source namespace and source ID) belongs to one active client: a second client claiming it is refused, so a search by it finds one client.
Other roles see what they saw before, the client's name, never this workspace or the terms.

Finance searches at `GET /api/gauge/clients?q=` and on the Engagements page: PO numbers, tags and external IDs (`system:id` or the bare ID) match whole and case-insensitively; names, legal names and contact names or emails match by contained text; merged duplicates are never results, and each result lists its linked engagements.
`client:merge` binds both clients' exact revisions and a reason.
Every engagement and opportunity of the duplicate moves to the surviving client as a new revision; approved economics stay frozen and later pricing follows the surviving client's rate cards.
A duplicate with client rate cards in force is refused until finance withdraws them (RATE-002), so no card silently changes whose work it prices.
Payment terms, approved days late and collection probability travel as one set: when the two sets differ, finance must choose the surviving or the duplicate client's set.

The survivor keeps its own legal name, tax ID reference and PO requirement, filling only empty ones from the duplicate, and gains the duplicate's contacts, addresses, exemption references, PO numbers, tags and every external identity (its recorded IDs and its import source), so searches by them find the survivor.
The duplicate stays as a merged record naming the survivor, reason, terms choice, operator and time; it takes no new engagement, opportunity, rate card, edit or second merge, and leaves every picker.
BASE-002 carries both records.

This obligation is done for every client field and door that exists today; SETUP-004 inherits client custom fields on this record, its search and merge before it ships, and INVOICE-001 inherits the bill-to contacts, addresses, PO requirement and client terms on issued invoices before invoices ship.
**Acceptance evidence:** Create two similarly named clients, merge the duplicate, search by PO and external ID, and verify terms and every linked project remain attached.

**SETUP-003 — Client billing currencies and exchange rates.** Finance keeps an owner-approved, effective-dated exchange-rate table for each currency to the USD reporting currency, recording rate, effective date, source (the accounting provider's rate or a named published rate) and approver.
An amount with no approved rate for its date stays shown unconverted, never as zero.
A new or corrected rate applies forward only: it never rewrites a conversion already used in a closed period (FINANCE-004) or on an issued document.
Realized FX gains and losses on settled payments remain with the accounting provider (BOUNDARY-001).
Client billing currencies, their end-to-end carriage and the conversion of portfolio, forecast and cash figures are SETUP-005.

Exact semantics (23 October 2026): only the owner approves a rate, recorded with its rate, effective date, source, reason, approver and approval time, and the owner's rates table on Access names who approved each rate and when; forward only means a new rate's effective date is on or after the latest approved rate for that currency and after the end of every currently closed agency period (FINANCE-004), an authorized reopen lifting that protection as it does for other dated financial facts; each amount converts at the latest rate effective on or before its date, a later approval winning a same-day correction.

**Acceptance evidence:** As the owner, approve CAD→USD 0.7300 effective 1 October from a named published rate and see the rates table show its rate, effective date, source and approver; approvals by finance or staff are refused.

An issued CAD 10,000.00 invoice dated in October converts to USD 7,300.00 labeled with the 0.7300 rate and its 1 October date, and a GBP amount dated before any approved GBP rate is shown unconverted, not zero, with the total withheld.
Approve 0.7400 effective 1 November and confirm the October converted total and the CAD invoice are unchanged; a backdated rate and a rate effective inside a closed period are refused.

**SETUP-004 — Custom fields on clients, engagements, people and tasks.** The owner defines custom fields on clients, engagements, people and tasks, typed as text, number, currency (with its ISO currency, SETUP-005), date, single select, multi select or person.
Select options can be added or retired without rewriting stored values; definitions are versioned and every value change keeps its history (GOVERN-005).
A field can be required on create, which is enforced on direct creation, on DELIVERY-003 template instantiation and on SALES-004 conversion.

Each field has a visibility level (everyone who can see the record, leads and finance, or finance only) enforced at the handler for pages, the API (CONNECT-020), CSV/XLSX/PDF exports, saved and scheduled reports and BI feeds (REPORT-004) and the client portal (CLIENT-001).
Every field is a filter and grouping dimension in REPORT-001, REPORT-002 and REPORT-004 and a filter in RESOURCE-002 resource search; number and currency fields can be summed as report measures.
Importers carry source field definitions and values with source IDs (MIGRATE-001, MIGRATE-004); a value that does not fit its field's type or options is reported in the preview, never dropped.
Whole-installation export and restore (BASE-002) include definitions and values.

Current doors use owner-defined, versioned visibility: a non-finance read requires both the current definition and the saved value's original definition version to permit it; explicitly saving a value under the current version is audited publication of that value.
Required fields apply at creation, including template tasks and conversion; adding a requirement never rewrites legacy records.

Native reports use whole-engagement cohorts for client/task/project fields and distinct-person capacity per utilization cohort; shared and multi-select cohorts overlap, currencies stay separate, and unset values remain unknown.
REPORT-004 and CLIENT-001 inherit these checks for future exports, scheduling, BI and portal doors.

**Acceptance evidence:** Import a Kantata OX package with a project single-select field "Practice" (Brand, Web) and a user field "Office" (NYC, Austin); the utilization and profitability reports grouped by Practice and by Office equal the totals of independent source reports from the same package, and a project carrying an undefined option "Legacy" is listed in the preview rather than dropped.
Make "Practice" required on engagements and see creation with it empty refused, both directly and through a SALES-004 conversion.
Add a finance-only currency field "Contract value": a lead cannot read it through the page, the API, a CSV export or a saved report, while finance sums it by Practice.
Filter resource search by Office = Austin and see only Austin people.

**SETUP-005 — Client currencies and converted figures.** Each client carries a default ISO 4217 billing currency (USD unless set), which an engagement may override before its first approved commercial version.

Rate cards (RATE-002), estimates and proposals (SALES-002, SALES-003), retainers (RETAINER-001), invoices and credits (INVOICE-001, INVOICE-004), QBO/Xero documents (CONNECT-001, CONNECT-002) and Stripe payment links (PAYMENT-001) carry that currency end to end; one document never mixes currencies.

Portfolio, forecast and cash figures (FINANCE-002, FINANCE-006, REPORT-001, REPORT-003) convert each amount at the rate effective on its transaction date and label the rate and date beside every converted total.
Conversion uses SETUP-003's approved rates.

Current semantics (23 October 2026): the portfolio's window earned value also reads in the reporting currency, each amount converted at the rate effective on its own date (approved time on its work date, reimbursable expenses on their date, milestones on their due date, retainer fees day by day as they accrue, overages on their period end) and labeled with each rate, date and source; its approved burn converts each cost in its own currency on its own date (time at its frozen cost on its work date, expenses on their date), and operational margin is converted earned value less converted burn; an amount with no rate stays unconverted and an unknown amount keeps its total, and the margin, unknown.

Expected cash on terms by month (FINANCE-002, FINANCE-007) converts each expected amount at the rate in force on the day it is expected (its receipt date, or the as-of day once past due); a month whose forecast is incomplete in any currency stays incomplete.

**Acceptance evidence:** Set a Toronto client to CAD and a New York client to USD; approve CAD→USD 0.7300 effective 1 October; issue a CAD 10,000.00 invoice and a USD 5,000.00 invoice in October and sync both to a QBO multicurrency sandbox, where each lands in its own currency; the October portfolio total reads USD 12,300.00 labeled with the 0.7300 rate and its 1 October date.

Approve 0.7400 effective 1 November and confirm the closed October total, the CAD invoice and its QBO copy are unchanged; a GBP amount dated before any approved GBP rate is shown unconverted, not zero.

**SALES-001 — Opportunity pipeline.** Leads track agency opportunities with stages, probability, owner, proposed start/end, services, expected value and staffing demand; won and lost outcomes retain history.
Open weighted pipeline is reported separately from won booked value, and tentative capacity remains visibly distinct from signed work.
A won opportunity linked to an engagement counts that engagement’s latest approved terms once, never both the opportunity and the terms.
Booked amounts are labeled "before billing".
Until billing exists, "booked backlog" means won value before billing; once invoices exist, backlog is booked value minus billed value.

Exact semantics (21 October 2026): per currency, *booked value* is the pipeline's booked value (latest approved terms per engagement, else its linked won value, plus unlinked wins, once each) labelled "before billing"; *billed* is the pre-tax total of native issued invoices dated on or before the report's as-of day on the engagements that carry booked value (never receipts, never other-currency invoices; issued credit notes net against it once INVOICE-004 ships, which inherits this); *backlog* = booked − billed in minor units, equal to booked value while nothing is issued and negative when billing exceeds it.
A billing packet is not an invoice.
Billed and backlog are finance-only (leads see booked value, which carries no invoice amounts) and each links to its invoice and booked sources (REPORT-005).
**Acceptance evidence:** Create two deals at different probabilities, move one to won, and verify that open weighted pipeline is reported separately from won booked value.
Link the won opportunity to an engagement with approved terms, approve revised terms, and verify that only the latest approved terms count once, never both the opportunity and the terms.
Verify booked amounts are labeled "before billing" and booked backlog equals won value before billing until billing exists; once invoices exist, reconcile backlog to booked value minus billed value.

**SALES-002 — Costed estimates.** Leads model service, role, hours, subcontractor and expense lines, rate assumptions, contingency, discounts and margin for hourly, fixed and mixed work; private costs remain finance-only.
Versions compare projected margin and feasible dates before sale.
An accepted estimate converts through SALES-004 into one engagement with its phase budgets, tasks and milestones.
Current native doors freeze the phase-start rate assumptions and calendar-only named-person feasibility per version; unknown cost/capacity remains unknown and prevents acceptance recording.
Fee contingency and customer discount use cumulative exact-cent allocation; expense allowances remain separate from fees.
Conversion prepares draft terms/milestones, tasks and unfilled role requests without committing staffing or issuing invoices.
Acceptance carrier (ct, 22 Oct): only the owner records reported external acceptance of the exact latest version.
The record holds the acceptor's name and contact as reported, the acceptance date, the channel (signed document, email, PO or verbal) and an evidence reference.
It is labelled 'recorded by agency, client identity unverified' on the estimate, engagement, budget, milestones, history and exports, and is never shown as client acceptance or a signature.
The owner may withdraw it, with an audit row, before conversion; after conversion, changes are change orders.
Finance or the owner then converts manually under fresh source assumptions and required SETUP-004 values.
When SALES-003 ships, its client-link or signed acceptance becomes the primary carrier, and attestation remains for offline acceptance only.
**Acceptance evidence:** Estimate design and engineering with a contractor and discount, compare versions and show a non-finance recipient no internal costs.
Accept a fixed-fee estimate, convert it twice, and find one engagement whose budget and milestones reconcile to that estimate (SALES-004).

**SALES-003 — Proposals and client acceptance.** Send a branded, versioned proposal with scope, deliverables, exclusions, dates, payment schedule and expiry; track delivery, viewing, questions and acceptance or rejection.
Bind accepted terms to the exact version and attach signed evidence from Docusign or Inkwell when signatures are needed.
Approved native email-confirmed client-link carrier (brief, 22 October): only the owner prepares, explicitly sends or revokes a complete immutable customer proposal.
The recipient must first confirm the invited email in a native operator account, without an internal Gauge staff grant.
The client door rechecks that exact recipient, the active releasing owner and the installation's release authority on every request; a link alone grants nothing.
A deliberate client POST binds the complete document fingerprint and exact latest estimate/proposal versions.
A superseded, expired or revoked version cannot receive a decision; questions and decisions retain history.
A changed price requires a new proposal and acceptance.

The GOVERN-008 sealed Resend connection and Base mail transport submit one version-bound durable manual send claim; provider submission is labelled separately from mailbox delivery, and an uncertain outcome never automatically retries.
Restore preserves documents, decisions and delivery history but strips recipient release authority; the new owner must explicitly authorize access again, without resending.
Client-link acceptance is the primary conversion carrier for released proposals; owner attestation remains for offline work.
A signature-required proposal cannot complete acceptance until verified provider evidence exists.

Current Inkwell intake reads its published envelope/artifact API with sealed read-only credentials, verifies native completed status, the exact recipient signing event and original/signed/certificate digests, and retains the signed PDF and certificate.
Client acceptance remains a deliberate exact-version POST; evidence intake never accepts automatically.
Gauge generates a complete immutable original PDF for a signature-required version, with the customer document fingerprint.
Only the native owner downloads it before release and binds that exact digest to Inkwell; a different PDF digest is refused even when the owner attests to it.
The provider original, signed PDF and certificate are read and digest-checked.
One envelope at the same Inkwell origin cannot bind another proposal version, even through a second connection.
The already-approved recipient carrier then confirms the exact proposal; provider evidence alone never accepts it.
Resend readback reconciles known message IDs or an owner-supplied ID whose body proves the exact delivery reference; it never sends, follows redirects or retains arbitrary provider bodies.
Delivered, bounced and unconfirmed remain distinct.
CONNECT-018 inherits this evidence and custody boundary; CONNECT-019 and FOLLOWUP-004 inherit readback/recovery before adding providers or scheduling.
**Acceptance evidence:** Send two proposal versions to a controlled inbox; accept the latest through the client link and require a fresh acceptance after changing its price.

**SALES-004 — Won work becomes an engagement.** Convert accepted estimates or won CRM deals into scoped work, phase budgets, tasks, milestones, staffing requests and invoice schedules with stable links back to the deal and accepted terms; required SETUP-004 fields must be supplied or mapped from the deal before conversion; replays create no duplicate.
The exact rules (ct, 19 October 16:47Z): today's carrier is a native SALES-001 won opportunity.

Finance or the owner converts it with `opportunity:convert`, which atomically creates one client engagement (the opportunity's name and client, its owner as lead, agency currency and time zone, no members) linked both ways (`engagement.opportunityId`, `opportunity.engagementId`), a draft fixed-fee budget for the won value with the won demand as effort (approved separately under BUDGET-001; no milestone is invented), and one open resource request per comma-listed service over the inclusive won dates.
Demand splits evenly by service, then by every date, in whole seconds rounded down; the remainder is recorded and shown as unplaced seconds.
Converting again, or replaying, returns the same engagement; an opportunity already linked to an engagement converts to that engagement.
Conversion moves booked value to the engagement and never counts it twice.

SALES-002 (accepted estimates with phase budgets, tasks and milestones), CONNECT-011 (CRM deals), SETUP-004 (required fields mapped before conversion) and RETAINER-005/INVOICE-002 (invoice schedules) inherit conversion before they ship.

**Acceptance evidence:** Win a fixed-fee opportunity, convert it twice, and find one engagement whose draft budget and staffing requests reconcile to the won value and demand, with any unplaced remainder shown.

**SALES-005 — Change scope with the client.** Track scope requests, baseline differences, schedule and margin impact, internal review and client acceptance; no pending change consumes approved client budget or authorizes billing.
Retain signed change evidence beside prior terms.
Current internal review boundary (ct, 25 October 2026): preparation by a native owner or finance person requires independent internal review by a different owner or finance person.
One person cannot self-review through another role or account.
Internal approval is labelled as such wherever shown and grants no client acceptance or business-effect authority.
Current native change carrier (default adopted pending ct):
the native owner explicitly releases one exact independently internally approved version to a confirmed non-staff recipient for one to 30 days.
The recipient opens it from the invited project or with a separately shared shown-once key.
The closed customer document preserves prior and proposed scope, currency, commercial allowances, effort, rounding, expenses and dates, without private cost or margin.
Acceptance requires a typed name and explicit consent through the native email-confirmed account and records the exact document digest, version, revision, recipient, reason and time.
Rejection retains its exact reason and never signs acceptance.
Only the native owner deliberately adopts the current accepted version, once, after live authority and complete baseline checks in the committing transaction.
Adoption changes only its exact native effects and retains prior terms and signature references; it never issues an invoice.
Internal approval keeps its internal label.
No message sends automatically, and restored evidence carries no review or adoption authority.
Native identity-bound evidence is not an external signature-provider or legal-compliance claim.
**Acceptance evidence:** Propose extra work, decline it, revise and accept it as the client, then verify only the accepted increment changes the forecast.

**RATE-002 — Client rate cards and cost policy.** Finance versions client, service, role and person rate cards, with effective dates, overtime rules, write-downs and negotiated overrides; an explain view shows precedence and approval freezes the chosen values.
W-2 loaded costs and 1099 contractor costs are declared inputs, not payroll calculations.
Each client rate card is denominated in that client's billing currency (SETUP-005); cost rates stay in USD.
Publish precedence among entry, project, client-role, role, person and service overrides.
Precedence is published as follows.

Bill rate: a finance-set entry override (with reason), then project, client-role, client, role, person and service cards; costs: person, role and service cards only (client and project cards carry bill rates).
Within a level, a card naming the entry's service beats an "All services" card, then the latest effective date on or before the work date wins.
Bill cards are in the client's billing currency, which is the agency currency until SETUP-005 gives clients their own (SETUP-005 inherits client-currency cards).
Declared costs are USD per hour, labeled W-2 loaded for employees and 1099 contract for contractors.
Cards saved before RATE-002 keep their single legacy currency.
Costs in different currencies are kept in separate buckets and are never summed without SETUP-003 rates.
